title: Field liaison & hotfix conductor for model degradation incidents
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define a single operational playbook and field-liaison responsibilities for incidents where a model rollout (hosted, dedicated, or private) shows behavioral regressions or increased error/latency rates. This ticket standardizes triage choreography, short-term remediation actions that minimize customer disruption, and the handoff to a longer-term postmortem and bugfix delivery path.
acceptance_criteria: A runbook exists that covers detection, triage, mitigation, customer communication, and postmortem handoff for regressions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments
An identified on-call field liaison role (contactable via PagerDuty) with a clear checklist for customer-facing communication and escalation
A hotfix conductor checklist that engineering can run to safely apply binary/model fixes or revert model versions with KV cache and routing reconciliation
Automation templates (runbooks / GitHub PR templates / Slack snippets) are added to the incident-docs repo and linked from Console incident UI
At least one tabletop drill executed with Platform, SRE, Support, and Solutions Engineering and notes captured
runbook_steps: Detection: alert fired from canary-quality-job or per-model quality regression detector (metric thresholds: top-1 prompt degrade >10% or token-error-rate rise >0.5% over 15m)
Initial triage (Field liaison): confirm scope (model variant / tenant / region / capacity tier) using trace-id and request sampling from Console traces
Customer impact assessment: map affected customers via tenant tagging and rate-limited query of usage exports; tag P0 customers in incident bridge

Containment options (choose one): 1) pin traffic to previous verified model variant on routing layer 2) apply live throttling for affected tenant slices 3) enable synthesis fallback to cheaper/robust variant via split-route policy
KV cache reconciliation: if rolling back model versions, invoke kvcache-rekey job to avoid stale keys; run validation queries against synthetic prompt set before un-slicing traffic
Hotfix application: if bug is config/serving-layer, apply change using canary enabled for 5% tenant slices for 10 minutes, inspect latency/error traces, then progressive increase
Rollback path: if canary shows regressions, trigger orchestrated revert and verify KV cache consistency and request-routing logs
Customer communication: craft initial notification with estimated impact, mitigation steps, and ETA; post updates every 30 minutes while incident is active
Post-incident: capture timeline, root cause hypothesis, short-term patch, and next-actions; schedule bugfix PR with owner and ETA within 72 hours
rollback_strategy: Non-disruptive model reversion: route traffic back to the last ‘verified’ model tag via routing policy and keep a 2x sampling rate of requests to the problematic variant for forensic logs
Configuration toggles: prefer config roll-forward (feature-gate off) when safe; if not, revert deploy in the same deployment window

Cross-plane coordination: when Private/VPC customers are affected, notify the private-deploy eng liaison to run the on-prem reversion play (requires offline package and customer approval where needed), and coordinate timing
KV cache safety: perform kvcache-stale-detect and run rehydration with synthetic seeds; if mismatch rate >2% hold traffic and reconcile
Customer-scoped rollbacks: for dedicated pools, consider tenant-specific routing overrides to avoid global rollbacks when impact is localized
communication_templates: Initial Slack/Email: 'Incident: model behavior regression detected for model {model_name} in {region}. Impact: {estimated_customers} customers may see degraded output. Mitigation in progress: routing to prior variant and KV reconciliation. Next update: {in_30_minutes}. Field liaison: {liaison_name}.'

Status update: 'Update: canary rollback initiated at {time}. Observed error-rate change: {metric_before} -> {metric_after}. Expected full mitigation ETA: {eta}. Actions: kvcache rekey in progress. Customer page updated: {status_page_url}.'

Postmortem summary: 'Resolved: degraded behavior for {model_name} was mitigated by routing to verified variant and applying a patch. Root cause: {short_root_cause}. Customer impact: {num_customers} customers affected for {duration}. Follow-ups: see next-actions.'
